messages.subject: cov_exp_quad performance test
parts:
Hi folks,

Now that RStan 2.12 is out with access to the Stan 2.12 cov_exp_quad() function, I thought I'd see how it fares against computation of the covariance matrix by hand. In case anyone is interested, here's a gist of the comparison:

https://gist.github.com/mike-lawrence/80527460403b8c907d3f21ce99f34786

I seem to be getting a 10% or so improvement with cov_exp_quad(). Is that about as expected?

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] cov_exp_quad performance test
parts:
real eta_sq_plus_noise ;
eta_sq_plus_noise = (eta^2) + noise ;

rho = 1/inv_rho ;

covMat = cov_exp_quad(x,eta,rho) ;

...
for(n in 1:N){
covMat[n,n] = eta_sq_plus_noise ;
}

I think you can replace all of the above (and remove
the declaration of rho) with:

covMat = cov_exp_quad(x, eta, inv(inv_rho));
for (n in 1:N)
covMat[n, n] = covMat[n, n] + noise;

I take it cov_exp_quad doesn't have a way to add jitter, which
seems like a drawback given that the noise term here is just
a scalar so there are shared derivative calcs.

- Bob
